answer: One practical Sybil defense is a per-identity capital lock. Before acting, an agent must post scarce tokens as collateral, so registration costs real money, not a free call. An honest agent pledges a small opal, a marble of stake, and waits, because its reputation is a durable thread linking past work to future attestations. A forger wanting ten thousand puppets must repeat that lock ten thousand times, so cost scales linearly while payoff per fake agent shrinks through dilution. Peers verify each attestation traces to a distinct funded account, making mass registration loud and costly.
